label: verify-pp-meeting-notes-decoder

claims.claim: The .life/.organism files hold no locomotion, sensor, actuator, behaviour or light vocabulary
claims.source_says: My grep of organism-format found only 'behaviour' in code comments and 'flight surface' in a scope note; no locomotion, sensor, actuator, stimulus, kinematics or optogenetic terms.
claims.note: Gap holds for locomotion/sensor/actuator, but the word 'behaviour' appears in comments (not as format vocabulary) and I did not read the spec files line by line.

claims.claim: Levin's lab states light-evoked behaviour in neurobots is a next step, so no optogenetic steering result is shown in public sources found
claims.source_says: Assessing presence of light- and other sensory-evoked behaviors in neurobots is an important next step.
claims.note: Quote reproduces on the Wyss page; the 'none found' part is a negative search result.

claims.claim: Anthropic AI for Science credits are up to $20,000 for 6 months, so '3 million tokens' is not that program's stated unit
claims.source_says: If successful, we will apply up to $20,000 in API credits to your account for a 6-month period.

claims.claim: Formlabs lists 72 materials, so '10 materials' is a subset
claims.note: Page shows 72 results under the current filters; the 'subset' inference is reasonable but the page was only read to 100000 of 139970 characters.

overall: Three of four claims reproduce from the sources (Wyss quote, $20,000 for 6 months, 72 results). The vocabulary-gap claim is mostly right but a loose grep still finds 'behaviour' in code comments.
